title: Intimacy Pact
concept: An agreement for initiating and declining physical closeness, so saying no never costs either of you anything, and what each of you actually wants doesn't stay a guess.
whenToUse: Set it up in advance, when initiating or declining feels tense, when it's stalled for weeks, or after a breach that touched this part of the relationship.
steps: Before you initiate, or before you say no, picture how it'll land for the other person — not just what you want in the moment.
Say out loud: neither of you will punish, sulk, or guilt-trip the other for declining. A no costs nothing.
Agree on a warm-no script you'll actually use, plus one real alternative — holding each other, a kiss goodnight, five minutes of talking — that still says "I want you, just not that, not tonight."
Each of you names what you actually enjoy and how you like to be approached — asked out loud or read from body language, morning or night.
Revisit the agreement every 30 days. Update it as things change — it's not a one-time contract, and nobody keeps score in between.
If a no has been met with guilt-tripping or pressure, or safety is genuinely in question, stop here and run Green Rule or Trust Recovery first — don't try to patch intimacy on top of that.

phrases.text: I want to be close — not in that space tonight. Can we hold each other?
Not about you. Can we do something together instead?
Not tonight — I do want to be near you. Is that okay?

working: A warm no, plus a real alternative — no cold shoulder, no guilt trip. Next time goes fine, because both people actually use the agreement.
notWorking: A no that gets a flat “fine” and the silent treatment — or someone initiating without a thought for whether the other person is actually up for it. That's what makes this feel unsafe to be honest about.
activity: Write the agreement together — there's a worksheet for this — and put a real date on the calendar for the 30-day check-in.
